#1778. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1775. Elche vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 14:48, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:51

Real Betis will aim to make it successive wins in Spain's top flight when they continue their campaign against Elche at Estadio Martinez Valero on Sunday afternoon.

The visitors posted a 2-1 victory over Malaga in their last league match, while Elche will enter the contest off the back of a 1-0 home defeat to Valencia.

Elche boast a record of two wins, four draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 10 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

The Green-Striped Ones were beaten 1-0 by Valencia in their last match, but that proved to be their first loss in five games in all competitions.

Martin Anselmi's side have actually won two of their last three matches, including a 3-1 victory over Pinatar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Elche have struggled in their recent meetings with Real Betis, losing four of the last five fixtures between the two sides, but the corresponding game last season finished 1-1.

The Green-Striped Ones have not managed to overcome Real Betis since April 2022, while their last home success over the Seville outfit came back in November 2009.

Real Betis lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 24 wins to Elche's 16, while 17 of their 57 games have finished all square.

Manuel Pellegrini's side were in Champions League action during the week, suffering a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in the league stage of the competition.

The Seville outfit were 2-1 winners over Malaga last time out, with that success making their record seven wins, two draws and two defeats from their 11 league matches this season, which has left them fourth in the table on 23 points.

Real Betis are only four points off third-placed Real Madrid and are, as expected, firmly in the Champions League picture at this stage of the La Liga campaign.

El Glorioso have a record of two wins, two draws and one defeat from their five away league matches this season, scoring six times and conceding seven.

Elche will be without the services of Marc Aguado and Thomas Lemar for this weekend's match through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong form.

Yago Santiago and Gonzalo Villar had both been doubts for this contest, but the pair are available for selection, while Pedro Bigas should also again be in the squad.

Lemar's position in the starting side is likely to be taken by Facundo Buonanotte, while there will be a spot through the middle for Fer Nino, who has netted six times in La Liga this season.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez remains on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back in the fold for the Seville outfit until the end of November.

Facundo Bernal is still suspended, but Junior Firpo and Alvaro Fidalgo are both expected to be back in the squad after recent absences.

Troy Parrott has not scored for Real Betis since the start of September, but the 24-year-old is expected to continue through the middle for Pellegrini's team.

Dituro; Sangare, Chust, Redondo, Revivo; Villar, Morcillo; Cepeda, Buonanotte, Valera; Nino

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Roca, Fornals; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

Elche have been in solid form of late, and this is not a straightforward match for Real Betis, but we are backing the Seville outfit to secure a valuable three points on Sunday.

#1774. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1773. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe, Palestra, Colwill, Palmer, Gittens, Essugo, Pedro, Hato, Fofana, Estevao, Lavia.Substitutes: Tosin, Delap, Sarr, Anselmino, Watson, Nicoll-Jazuli, Kellyman, Acheampong, Curd, Satpayev, Subuloye, Walsh, Emenalo, Kavuma-McQueen

#1771. Nicky Butt doubles down on Michael Carrick's 'management's not for me' claim - as he pinpoints moment under-fire Man United boss made comment

Published: 07:20 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 07:21 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford.

Carrick, 45, returned to the club where he earned legendary status as a player in January in the aftermath of Ruben Amorim's sacking.

Despite a strong end to last season when he guided United to third place, Carrick is under huge pressure this time around after picking up just seven points from nine matches.

Speaking last month, Butt revealed that Carrick had told him he would only return to management for the United job after his sacking by Middlesbrough in June 2025, a claim the current Red Devils boss subsequently laughed off.

Yet, Butt, appearing on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan, has reaffirmed his stance and pinpointed the exact moment when Carrick told him he didn't want to get back in the dugout.

'I believe I said that but I’ll clarify what I meant,' Butt said. 'And I’m not ducking it, I’m really not, I’ll explain. I was playing in a padel tournament with Michael, he’s my doubles partner, and I was talking about football and Middlesbrough.

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford

Speaking on Football Uncensored, Butt revealed the exact moment that Carrick made the claim

'I had a beer after it, and I was like "so what’s your plans mate? What do you think you’re going to do when you get back into management?"

'He said "no, it’s all over the show, it’s hard work – however, if the big one came up, obviously I would take it".'

Butt continued: 'And the big one did come up, and he took it, and that wasn’t a case of me saying Michael didn’t want the Man United job, it was a case of he didn’t want a job.

'He didn’t want to go driving up and down the M6 all day when he’s got kids at home for no reward.

'But if the big one comes, which I assume was Man United, then he’d take it. That’s the facts of the conversation that I had with him.'

When pressed on Butt's comments ahead of United's draw with Leeds last month, Carrick had said: 'I definitely wouldn't be here if that was the case, would I? At this stage, it's the best job and the best role I could possibly have.

'I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here.

'I'm loving it. I love the situation when actually you get some sort of struggle and you've got to find a way out of it. I actually enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success.

'If you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it, and I'm enjoying it as we go.'

Butt claimed Carrick said he'd only return to management for 'the big job' at Man United

Butt's original claim had come on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast when he said: 'I was with Michael before he got the Man United job and spoke to him about management.

'He went "no it's not for me, it's too much, my head's all over the show, I'd only do it for the big job. The big job is Man United".

'So because that club's gone to him he's naturally going to go and do it. I think when he's gone through that door, put aside last year because like Scholesy said that's totally different to this year, I think he's realised he's gone into a club that's different to the club that he knew and was at.

'But these lads won't turn down Man United. Ole Gunnar (Solskjaer) wouldn't turn it down.

'Roy Keane might never turn that down. When that club comes calling and you've been at that football club, you don't turn it down.'

United and Carrick face a crunch week, with home games against Roma and Aston Villa coming ahead of next week's international break.

#1768. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1767. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

Home » Home 2 » Aston Villa vs Chelsea FC: Possible Lineups, Stats, Prediction & Odds | English Premier League

Aston Villa will play their first Premier League game since the departure of manager Remi Garde by mutual consent earlier in the week. Assistant manager Eric Black has taken over the reins at Villa Park and the Scot will look to salvage whatever he can from this season, with his side needing a miracle to avoid relegation. It is understood that Black is to stay caretaker manager till the end of the season or until Villa are able to appoint a new full-time manager.

Chelsea will see the likes of Willian, Cesc Fabregas, Pedro and Gary Cahill among others returning from international duty and will look to hit the ground running following the break.

Since taking over from Jose Mourinho, Guus Hiddink has been able to to provide some much needed stability to what looked like a fast sinking Chelsea ship. However, the Blues sit 10th in the league table, with European competition looking increasingly unlikely next season. As such, Chelsea supporters have been clamouring for the likes of Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Kenedy and Bertrand Traore to get more game time for the rest of the campaign.

Possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Guzan; Hutton, Clark, Cissokho, Lescott; Westwood, Guey; Gil, Veretout, Ayew; Gestede

Possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Terry, Cahill, Ivanovic, Azpilicueta; Mikel, Fabregas; Oscar, Willian, Pedro; Remy

Aston Villa 1 – 3 Chelsea It should be a comfortable victory for Chelsea if they were to play to their potential and with some endeavour — something that hasn’t been seen too often from the West London outfit this season. Nothing but victory should suffice for Chelsea but with the way things have gone this season, it wouldn’t be too surprising if Villa came away with something from this tie.

#1763. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1762. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

On the front foot 👊 pic.twitter.com/AZC7UXYXrj

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

The fans are out in force in Hong Kong, where the Premier League continues to dominate attention.

Here’s what the former striker told Manchester City: “I’m looking forward to it. I’m not sure Enzo is going to change that much but some tweaks here and there.

“People talking about it being similar to when [Alex] Ferguson left but I don’t think it’s the same, they didn’t have the same infrastructure. He’s a top manager. He will want to put his own stamp on it.”

The biggest story in football right now is increasingly hard to ignore.

Gianni Infantino’s ludicrous plan was sunk almost as soon as it was announced, then he defended himself with such verve as to make himself look completely isolated and apart from the organisation itself, and now UEFA has said it is calling time.

The governing body says it has lost faith in the Peace Prize inventor, a problem which had been in the post for a while now.

The two London sides are facing off in their own pre-season friendly.

You can follow that live here, and find out which player has been sent off.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

The venue in Hong Kong is decent enough and has started filling out. It’s a jaunty 26 degrees, 92% humidity, and raining too. It’s just like being in London during your worst nightmares, basically.

We’ll see how this continues, and if it does continue, over the coming weeks, but Phil Foden has the nod as captain for Enzo Maresca tonight.

Foden signed a new contract recently but has been well off his consistent best for some time now. Another poor season would put him in the frame for the exit door next summer, so this is a chance.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#1760. Man United Confidential: Club on red alert to prevent repeat of shocking Roma violence, why football insiders doubt Unai Emery is right fit for Old Trafford and meet the 17-year-old lighting up Darren Fletcher's impressive youth team

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 09:07 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 09:16 EDT, 3 November 2026

Manchester United are on high alert to prevent Roma fans infiltrating the areas of Old Trafford reserved for home supporters in tonight’s Champions League clash.

The fixture has a history of violence and United are determined to make sure more trouble isn’t sparked by Italian ultras buying tickets in the United sections of the stadium.

There were flashpoints when Galatasaray visited Old Trafford in October 2023, and again when Rangers were in town last year after tickets fell into the wrong hands.

There were concerns that the risk of unrest might be heightened by tickets for recent United games going on general sale, but the club insist they are only allocated to fans who were on their database prior to the Champions League draw being made.

The same restrictions apply to supporters forwarding season tickets and all hospitality guests whose tickets have been checked individually before being issued.

However, United will be extra vigilant to prevent Roma fans ending up among the home supporters, with any stray travelling fans being ejected immediately.

The rivalry between United and Roma dates back to their first meeting in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans

United won the return leg of the quarter-final 7-1, with police making 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford

The official allocation for the Italian club is 3,300, and those fans will congregate at Shambles Square in the city centre before making their way to Old Trafford under close police supervision.

Confidential understands Roma have avoided trouble playing away in Serie A and Europe this season after the Italian football authorities restricted travel for most of their teams.

With the exception of their games against Como and Udinese, Roma have only been allowed to take fans who live outside the Lazio region and are more likely to be affiliated to official fan clubs than the hardcore ultras who live in the centre of Rome.

The rivalry between United and Roma dates back to their first meeting in the quarter-final of the Champions League in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans after they reacted to being pelted with missiles by Roma supporters.

A number of United fans were hospitalised, including 10 who were stabbed after being ambushed outside the Stadio Olimpico before kick-off. Roma were fined £31,000 – twice as much as United – and The Independent Manchester United Supporters’ Association pursued legal action against the Italian police for years afterwards.

United won the return leg 7-1, with police making 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford. Sir Alex Ferguson’s side knocked Roma out of the quarter-finals again the following season on their way to winning the Champions League, having also played each other in the group stage – when trouble flared in Rome and three fans were stabbed.

Wayne Rooney scores United's third goal in that 7-1 thrashing. Michael Carrick also got on the scoresheet twice

The most recent meeting between the two clubs, in the Europa League semi-final in 2021, was played behind closed doors due to Covid.

A GMP spokesperson said: 'Greater Manchester Police is expecting a number of Roma supporters arriving into Manchester today with officers at the airport and would like to offer a warm welcome to all supporters.

'We are highly experienced in policing high-profile events and have been working closely with both clubs and supporters to ensure everyone can enjoy the match safely. We understand the majority of supporters attend matches peacefully however if there are any issues of disorder, we have a full plan in place to deal with concerns and will take action appropriately.

'There will be police in and around Old Trafford, so if you have any concerns before, during or after the match, then please speak to officers or stewards.'

The United squad flew back from London after Saturday’s defeat by Chelsea, avoiding the rail chaos that piled more misery onto their suffering fans.

Michael Carrick and the players took the train from Stockport to Euston on Friday, but returned by plane following the 2-0 loss. They were back at Carrington and heading for home by the time many supporters were left stranded by widespread delays caused by a points failure at Camden.

Confidential understands only one train left Euston for Manchester on Saturday evening and that was rammed with passengers desperate to get home and avoid having to pay for a hotel stay.

British Transport Police had to intervene to calm several disturbances before the train left Euston after standing still on the platform for half an hour, finally arriving at Manchester Piccadilly well after midnight.

Carrick and his players had a miserable time at Stamford Bridge on Saturday - but they did at least avoid the train chaos that affected the club's fans

When it comes to Ineos and the footballing decisions at United, much is made about the ‘best in class’ structure they have supposedly put in place.

There is Jason Wilcox as director of football, Christopher Vivell as director of recruitment, with figures like Michael Sansoni, director of data, key to the Ineos eco-system at Old Trafford. Omar Berrada is CEO and Sir Jim Ratcliffe is very hands-on as minority owner.

Carrick slotted into that set-up as head coach without ruffling any feathers. Should he get the boot, it’s fair to question if the structure is actually fit for purpose.

Chatting to Confidential in recent days, sources in the game explained why the current structure would not necessarily suit someone like Unai Emery.

As one of the best managers in the Premier League, Emery should be a dream target if United are to move on from Carrick in the coming weeks. He is, it is understood, on a five-man shortlist of potential replacements.

But Aston Villa boss Emery, for example, is said to choose his own sporting director and deal directly with ownership – rather than a director of football or a CEO – given the immense power he wields.

Would Unai Emery be happy to work with the likes of Omar Berrada (left) and Jason Wilcox?

There are serious questions being asked of Wilcox and Berrada right now. What happens moving forward with Vivell is also an issue.

Which raises the question: if United pivot in the dugout in a bid to save this sorry season and they have any chance of landing a big fish like Emery, why would you stick to a system that wouldn’t be agreeable to one of the league’s very best managers?

Maybe the structure is the problem, after all.

It’s approaching half a century since United’s famous win over Liverpool in the 1977 FA Cup final denied Bob Paisley’s side the chance of winning the Treble, but the rivalry has paid off for the family of Emlyn Hughes.

When the two clubs met again at Wembley later that summer and shared the Charity Shield after a goalless draw, Liverpool’s captain and No 6 swapped shirts with his United counterpart Martin Buchan whose white Admiral jersey with the three vertical stripes sold for £10,000 at auction on Monday.

The shirt, which had an estimate of between £4-6,000, was one of 200 lots from Hughes’ career with Liverpool, Wolves and England which were auctioned off by Budds on behalf of his family. A Northern Ireland No 8 jersey worn by George Best also sold for £49,000.

Hughes, who died in 2004 at the age of 57, led the great Liverpool side that would have beaten United by 22 years to become the first English club to win the league title, European Cup and FA Cup in the same season were it not for Tommy Docherty’s team, captained by Buchan, beating them 2-1.

Almost 50 years later, the rivalry between the two clubs is still as strong as ever as United prepare to go to Anfield straight after the international break.

Finding slivers of positivity at United right now is far from easy, but Darren Fletcher’s Under 18s are doing their level best as their 10-game unbeaten run goes on.

Spearheaded by Kai Rooney, Noah Ajayi and Jaume Camacho, Fletcher’s fledglings have hit 38 goals in the past 10 games, scoring 16 in the past three alone with a 6-3 win over Liverpool followed up by a 6-0 win at Burnley and a 4-1 win at Blackburn.

Jaume Camacho, 17, is a real rising star and helping Darren Fletcher's Under 18s play some scintillating football

This was a squad overshadowed by the brilliance of JJ Gabriel last season and one that started this campaign without too much star power on paper.

But with Camacho, 17, a real rising star – his four goals against Liverpool were sublime – Fletcher’s side are playing some top football and dismantling teams the way other clubs are dismantling United's first team right now.

United have 99 problems, but Fletcher’s Under 18s aren’t one.

#1759. GdS: Milan search for ‘spark’ in Europe – how Amorim plans to harness post-derby ‘fuel’

After beating Inter in the derby on Saturday night, AC Milan are hoping that they can ride the wave and get back on track in Europe.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Milan want to rediscover their ‘international DNA’ and put behind them a start to the Europa League campaign that has seen one win and two defeats in the first three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While it is not yet a do-or-die situation for Ruben Amorim and his squad, failing to secure a win against the Hungarian side – who have a perfect record so far – would make reaching the top 24 significantly more difficult, and a top-eight finish nearly impossible.

Given that the Rossoneri have won seven Champions League titles, no other team in this European competition can boast such a trophy cabinet. Furthermore, the Portuguese manager reached the final with Manchester United two editions ago, ultimately losing to Tottenham.

Consequently, Milan and Amorim must ‘honour’ the Europa League in a manner far removed from their last away outing, which was a heavy defeat against European debutants Bournemouth, with Mike Maignan getting sent off.

This evening over 50,000 fans are expected at San Siro, including a sold-out away sector of 4,200, with over 5,000 Hungarian fans in total throughout the stadium. Milan must secure a victory, channelling the enthusiasm currently felt at Milanello following Saturday’s derby win.

The former United manager tried to brush it aside so his squad could focus solely on the Europa League, but the atmosphere during the final training session was as upbeat as it gets, with lots of ‘slaps’ of congratulations dished out.

Koni De Winter was patted on the back in celebration of his daughter’s birth, Diego Moreira was praised for his goal in the derby, Sankhoun Diawara was acknowledged for his debut(s), and even coach Carlos Fernandes got some love for the corner routine leading to Adrien Rabiot’s goal.

😂 A lot of slaps were given out before training: De Winter for the birth of his daughter, Pulisic for his renewal, Diawara for his debut and Carlos Fernandes for the corner routine leading to Rabiot’s goal ❤️🖤

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 4, 2026

The enthusiasm following the derby must now be channelled into focus and determination ahead of the Europa League return. Milan cannot afford another embarrassing performance in European competition, like those seen against Benfica and Bournemouth.

The club’s storied history forbids it, and Gerry Cardinale certainly wouldn’t welcome a repeat of those displays against the Portuguese or English sides. For this reason, while rotating the squad with an eye on Sunday’s match in Genoa, Amorim will ensure the team retains some key pillars.

De Winter will remain in defence, Yunus Musah and Rabiot in midfield, and Goncalo Ramos in attack. Compared to Saturday’s lineup, there will be seven changes including a forced one in goal, with Lorenzo Torriani replacing the suspended Maignan. Ardon Jashari steps in for Luka Modrić, who will be rested.

With six players sidelined due to injury, the scope for rotation is limited. Yet, even while fielding a side with a significantly lower average age than the one that played in the derby (23.6 years versus 28.1), Amorim has opted not to throw 18-year-olds Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto into the XI.

His goal is to help Gonçalo Ramos – who hasn’t managed a single shot on target in his last two appearances – regain his scoring touch. Consequently, Camarda will have to wait a little longer. As for Comotto, the midfield requires experience, and both Rabiot and Musah are too vital to be left out.

Across the 2024-25 Champions League and the current Europa League campaign, the Rossoneri have won only one of their last six matches, hardly the kind of record expected from a club with such a storied continental past.

According to UEFA, a win in the Europa League is worth €450,000 (with €150,000 for a draw), figures that pale in comparison to the rewards for similar results in the Champions League (€2.1m and €700k, respectively).

The total earnings at the end of each competition are also incomparable: Champions League finalists can rake in between €120m and €125m, whereas the winner of the Europa League can earn, at most, just over €40m.

However, securing the second-tier European trophy guarantees direct qualification for the 2027-28 Champions League, bypassing the need to finish in the top four of Serie A. It also grants a spot in the UEFA Super Cup, which awards €4m to each of the two participating clubs.

Returning to the Champions League – a major objective that was not achieved last season – must be achieved this year, not least for the sake of sponsorships and brand value, two areas of great importance to Cardinale.

Ultimately, the goal is to win a trophy, ideally the Scudetto. However, adding the Europa League title to the trophy cabinet would certainly be a welcome achievement, especially given Milan didn’t win it when it was the UEFA Cup either.

#1758. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.
